policy: Candidates rejected before admission remain permanently addressable so they are not rediscovered under new names.

entries.title: Single Scalar SAT Invariant
entries.reason: No exact invariant, computation rule, or falsification condition was specified; the idea merely renamed the desired decision procedure.
entries.salvage: Specify a finite representation, a polynomial evaluation algorithm, and an explicit family on which equal invariant values would contradict the claim.

entries.title: Deterministic Isolation Alone Decides SAT
entries.reason: Isolation can promise uniqueness conditioned on existence but does not by itself decide whether any satisfying assignment exists or recover one deterministically.
entries.salvage: H047 adds a deterministic family of hashes plus a certified tractable class for every isolated residual.

entries.title: Projected Bounded-Treewidth Lift for Every CNF
entries.reason: A universal polynomial-size projected bounded-treewidth representation would compile to a polynomial-size DNNF after forgetting auxiliaries, conflicting with explicit DNNF lower-bound families under the stated unrestricted representation promise.
entries.salvage: Restrict the input class or use a target representation not efficiently closed to ordinary DNNF under forgetting.

entries.title: PIT in P Directly Implies P Not Equal NP
entries.reason: Known hardness-versus-randomness consequences of deterministic PIT yield a Boolean-or-arithmetic circuit lower-bound disjunction, not an immediate separation of P and NP.
entries.salvage: H039 records the exact win-win consequence and treats it as a barrier-breaking intermediate lemma.

entries.title: NEXP Circuit Lower Bound Directly Separates P and NP
entries.reason: A lower bound for an exponential-time class does not by itself place an explicit NP language outside P.
entries.salvage: H057 retains Circuit-SAT algorithms only as an intermediate route toward stronger lower bounds and H030.

entries.title: Polynomially Bounded Proofs Have Polynomial-Time Search
entries.reason: Existence of polynomial-size proofs does not imply that those proofs can be found deterministically in polynomial time.
entries.salvage: H046 separately requires short proofs, deterministic verification, and a complete polynomial-time search algorithm.

entries.title: Finite SAT Benchmarks Establish a Universal Polynomial Algorithm
entries.reason: Any finite benchmark suite can falsify an implementation but cannot establish an asymptotic worst-case polynomial bound.
entries.salvage: Use finite experiments only to destroy concrete universal algorithms, never to promote them to theorem status.

entries.title: Free Semantic Canonicalization of Residual Formulas
entries.reason: An unspecified canonicalizer can hide SAT solving, equivalence testing, or exponential precomputation inside one uncharged operation.
entries.salvage: H040 fixes a certificate language and charges the complete canonicalization computation.

entries.title: Finite Local Rules Are Automatically Non-Universal
entries.reason: Finite bounded-radius transition systems can simulate general computation; locality alone does not provide a structural invariant or block solve-and-encode behavior.
entries.salvage: Characterize the semantic closure of the exact finite grammar, as required by H043-H045 and their adversarial bridges.

entries.title: Random Hard Formulas Count as an Explicit Family
entries.reason: High-probability hardness of random formulas does not supply a deterministic polynomial-time constructible infinite family.
entries.salvage: Derandomize the construction or provide an explicit pseudorandom generator with a proved preservation theorem, as demanded by H053.

entries.title: Linear or SDP Lift with Uncharged Coefficients
entries.reason: Exponential information may be hidden in real precision or coefficient bit length unless all numerical resources are explicitly charged.
entries.salvage: Require polynomial encoding length, rational coefficients, and explicit extraction complexity in every lift statement.

entries.title: Interesting Open Problem Without a Proof Route
entries.reason: The candidate named a legitimate open problem but did not state how proving or refuting it would advance a registered path toward P versus NP or eliminate a central mechanism.
entries.salvage: Add an exact proof_role, a downstream theorem, and a falsifiable next_gate before readmission.
